To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the printing performance of coated papers is strongly affected by calendering conditions, and the type of pigment used in the coating formulation.
the print density increases with the increase of supercalender pressure, temperature and plastic pigment.
the printing performance of coated paper can be improved by incorporating plastic pigments into the coating layer, and that this improvement is dependent on the supercalendering process conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a better understanding of the factors that control the print performance of coated paper and board, and in particular the role of supercalendered structure and coating composition.
the development of an understanding of the factors that influence the printability of paper and board, in terms of both print quality and print speed.
the effects of supercalender conditions on the structure of the coatings, and the effects that these changes in structure have on printing properties, particularly print gloss.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the printing properties of coated papers, particularly those coated with pigmented coatings, are significantly affected by the supercalendering parameters, with the influence being greater in coatings containing plastic pigmented than in those containing clay.
the effects of supercalendered conditions and pigment types on gravue printing performance are related to the effects of these variables on coating structure.

1. the effects of increasing super-calendering pressure and temperature are to increase the density of the coating layer and to improve the surface smoothness; 2. incorporation of hollow plastic pigmented into the coating layer improves printing performance, particularly when the coating layer is subjected to high levels of super-calendering; and 3. the effect of plastic pigments on print density is dependent on the type of pigment used in the coating layer.

1. the influence of supercalender pressure and temperature on gravure print performance can be explained in terms of changes in coating structure, and 2.
the use of plastic pigments in combination with calendering conditions that are optimized for their unique behaviour, can result in coatings with enhanced printing properties.

the effects of supercalender conditions on gravure print density and quality can be understood by considering the influence of the supercalender on coating structure, and the influence of the coating structure on the gravure printing process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to improve the gravure print performance of coated paper by the appropriate choice of supercalender conditions and the incorporation of hollow plastic pigment into the coating layer.

the use of hollow plastic pigmented coatings in gravure printing can improve gravure print quality, and this is due to the unique effects of calendering conditions and the presence of the hollow thermoplaistic pigments in the coatings.
